lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with New Orleans businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. New Orleans has two audiences that rarely overlap: visitors who decide within hours where to eat, drink and listen, and residents who choose a roofer, a doctor or a school with great care. We build separate plans for each and time them to the city's calendar.

sections.heading: Visitors and locals are two different markets
paragraphs: Tourism and conventions are the city's best-known business. Guests arrive for Carnival, for festivals, for a meeting at the convention centre or before a cruise, and they choose restaurants, tours, bars and music venues from a phone while standing on the pavement. For these businesses the deciding factors are the map listing, recent reviews, photos, opening hours that are actually correct and a booking link that works.

Residents behave differently. They ask neighbours, read reviews closely and stay with the businesses they trust for years. Messaging, ad targeting and even posting times should reflect which group pays your bills.

sections.heading: Neighbourhoods people actually search for
paragraphs: New Orleans is a city of named neighbourhoods and people use those names in search. The French Quarter and the Marigny hold much of the nightlife and music. The Central Business District and the Warehouse District have hotels, offices, museums and the convention centre. Uptown and the Garden District mean Magazine Street shopping, the universities and old residential streets. Mid-City, Lakeview, Gentilly, Bywater and Algiers each have their own customer base.

The metro extends well past the city line. Metairie and Kenner in Jefferson Parish hold a large share of the area's retail, medical offices and car dealers. The Westbank across the river and the Northshore across the lake are separate trips that many people will not make for an everyday service.
bullets: Pages for the neighbourhoods and parishes you serve, using the names locals use.
Ad targeting drawn around realistic travel, including the river and the lake as real barriers.
Listings on maps and travel platforms kept identical, down to holiday hours.

sections.heading: Planning around the New Orleans year
paragraphs: The calendar here drives revenue more than in most cities. Carnival builds for weeks to Mardi Gras day, and parade routes change which streets are reachable and which businesses are busy. Spring brings French Quarter Fest and Jazz Fest, and early summer has Essence Festival.

Late summer is the slow season for visitors, with heat and the peak of hurricane season. Many restaurants use those weeks for local promotions. We set budgets month by month against your own sales history, prepare festival content ahead of time, and keep a plan ready for storm closures so listings and ads reflect what is really open.

sections.heading: Beyond hospitality
paragraphs: The Port of New Orleans, the river trade, shipbuilding and energy firms support a business-to-business economy that needs plain, well-organised websites and search visibility for specific services. Old housing stock and a wet climate also mean constant work for roofers, foundation specialists, plumbers and restoration companies, who compete hard in map results.

cards.heading: Who we can help in New Orleans

items.title: Restaurants, bars and venues
items.text: Accurate listings, appetising photography, reservation links and short video timed to festivals and game days.

items.title: Tours and attractions
items.text: Swamp, history and cemetery tours win on reviews and on booking pages that work quickly on a phone.

items.title: Home repair and restoration
items.text: Roofing, foundation, plumbing and water damage firms need neighbourhood pages and call-focused ads.

items.title: Maritime and industrial firms
items.text: Suppliers to the port and river industries need clear service descriptions, certifications and contact routes.

items.title: Local food and retail brands
items.text: Pralines, coffee, spice blends and art sell to former visitors nationwide through a well-built online shop.

presence: TDM works with New Orleans businesses remotely. We have no office or team member in the city. Our team delivers strategy, design, development and video online, with scheduled calls and written reports.

faqs.q: Is TDM based in New Orleans?
faqs.a: No. We work with New Orleans businesses remotely. You deal with our team by video call and shared reporting.

faqs.q: When should a New Orleans business advertise most?
faqs.a: It depends on who you sell to. Visitor businesses usually spend more ahead of Carnival, the spring festivals and autumn, and less in late summer. Local service firms often see steadier demand, with spikes after heavy weather. We set the budget against your own sales pattern.

faqs.q: How do I get my restaurant found by tourists in the French Quarter?
faqs.a: Most visitors search the map for something nearby and open now. Keep your Google Business Profile complete, with current hours, menu and photos, collect reviews steadily and make sure the same details appear on travel and reservation sites.

faqs.q: How much do you charge for marketing in New Orleans?
faqs.a: The cost depends on the scope of work. We discuss your goals in a free consultation and then send a quote.

faqs.q: Can you market a business in Metairie or on the Northshore?
faqs.a: Yes. We treat each as its own area, with its own pages, business profile and ad targeting, because customers there search and travel differently from those in the city.
